summary: The model's predicted risk is a sigmoid of four terms added on the logit scale. A hinge on age and BMI together raises risk for older, heavier people (switching it off lowers the training AUC from 0.837 to 0.731); a hinge on income against score lowers risk when income is high relative to score (0.748 without it); a hinge on the visit count raises risk for frequent visitors, and smoking lowers its threshold and adds to it, so smoking matters mainly for frequent visitors (0.787 without it); a small, almost always-on linear term adds slight slopes in age, BMI and score (0.834 with it held at its mean). Female, urban, insured and noise carry small weights: replacing every edge from them by its mean contribution gives a training AUC of 0.8369.

recheck_notes: No mismatch and no needs_review item. The 24 unchecked free-text sentences carry no numbers (directions, structure and readings); each reading is backed by the probe, subgroup or ablation in the same hypothesis.
tool_bugs: get_formula on a leaf returned latex null (tractable false) without force=true even for a single 10-input ReLU unit; worked with force=true. Piping xn.py --calls into head killed the batch part-way (SIGPIPE), so only some splits were applied on the first try; reran the rest. A composition annotation is refused if its subgraph_nodes repeat the children's nodes; it validates with only its own nodes (the output) and the children's exits as entries. Not tool bugs as such: the evidence-narrative lint flags 'zero' in 'set to zero' (an ablation setting), fixed by rewording.

leaves.name: age_bmi_hinge
leaves.why: A joint age-and-BMI threshold above which predicted risk climbs, with a higher BMI lowering the age at which it starts; the age-by-BMI probe confirms the switch-on points.

leaves.name: linear_age_bmi_score
leaves.why: Read only as the direction of a small near-linear correction (risk up with age and BMI, down with score) plus the logit baseline; it adds little ranking information.

leaves.name: visits_smoker_hinge
leaves.why: Frequent visitors get higher risk and smoking lowers the visit threshold and adds to the hinge, so smoking matters mainly for frequent visitors; the visits-by-smoker probe and subgroup counts confirm it.

leaves.name: income_score_hinge
leaves.why: High income relative to score lowers predicted risk, with a higher score raising the income needed for protection; the income-by-score probe confirms it.

overall_function: The model adds four terms on the logit scale and applies a sigmoid. Risk rises once age and BMI together pass a threshold (the two trade off: heavier people reach it younger), and rises with the number of visits above a threshold, where smoking lowers that threshold and adds to the effect, so smoking matters mainly for frequent visitors. Risk falls when income is high relative to score: income is protective and a higher score cancels that protection. A small, almost always-on linear term adds slight slopes in age, BMI and score; female, urban, insured and noise carry small weights and barely change the prediction.
stuck: Little: a SIGPIPE from piping a batch into head stopped the input splits part-way (rerun), the composition annotation needed only its own node in subgraph_nodes, and leaf formulas needed force=true. The linear unit has no reading beyond its direction.
